summary.title: Deep Learning CNN's in Tensorflow with GPUs
summary.one_liner: You learn the basic architecture of a convolutional neural network, build a CNN in TensorFlow to classify MNIST handwritten digits (~98% accuracy at 10k iterations), and run training on an AWS GPU instance.
keywords: how to build a cnn in tensorflow
takeaways: CNNs combine convolution (feature extraction), pooling (dimensionality reduction) and fully connected layers to classify inputs.
Same padding preserves input width and height, while valid padding does not pad; ReLU adds non-linearity and sparsity.
Mini-batch training (batch size 128) with softmax cross-entropy loss is used to train the MNIST model for 10k iterations to reach about 98% accuracy.
TensorFlow prefers GPU placement by default when a GPU is available; the tutorial runs training on an AWS G2.2xlarge instance with a community AMI.
Code and data are available in the linked ColeMurray/tensorflow-cnn-tutorial GitHub repository.
summary.summary: The tutorial first explains CNN building blocks: convolution with kernels, strides and padding, ReLU activation, pooling, and fully connected layers. It then walks through creating a CNN in TensorFlow to train on the MNIST handwritten digit dataset, including data download, helper functions, inference, softmax cross-entropy loss, and a 10k-iteration train/evaluate loop reaching about 98% accuracy. The final section shows how to launch an AWS EC2 GPU instance with a TensorFlow AMI, sync code via rsync, and run training there, which takes about 20 minutes. The page is a hands-on tutorial with linked code and suggested next steps.
